The natural satellite of the Earth is the Moon.

To enrich the artistic concept of a novel set during the American Gold Rush, one might adapt elements from the Bluegrass music genre. The rapid, intricate picking of the banjo could mirror the frantic, relentless pace of prospectors digging for gold, while the driving rhythm of the fiddle might reflect the high stakes and adrenaline of the adventure. The raw, unpolished energy of the genre aligns with the rugged survival aspects of the era, and the traditional storytelling nature of bluegrass lyrics can help encapsulate the personal narratives of risk and the raw pursuit of wealth that defined this historic period.
